title: Encoder Resolution Reader
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Sensors for Robotics
description: Turn a shaft and change the number of encoder bits, and watch the step number, the step size and the reported angle on a dial with a magnified strip that shows single steps. Then solve five problems on step size, steps and degrees, and speed from two readings. Used in Chapter 5.

learningObjectives: Calculate the step size of an encoder, convert between encoder steps and degrees, and find a speed from two position readings, to within 1 percent, in five problems, with at least 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: See the steps appear on a magnified strip as the shaft turns, then apply the conversions to new numbers with an immediate check
keyQuestions: What happens to the size of one step when you add one bit?
Why does the reported angle sometimes differ from the shaft angle?
commonMisconceptions: More bits means a larger step
A fine encoder is an accurate joint
assessmentOpportunities: Five typed answers, one attempt each; 4 of 5 for mastery
